cohort.definition: ARCHETYPE RECORD — NOT A COMPANY. This file describes a typical developer-tools startup's entry-level hiring pattern, synthesized as an archetype for planning when no company-specific record exists. It must never be quoted as facts about any individual company.
cohort.time_window: listings and program pages live when checked, October 2026

data_sources.label: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook (computer and information technology occupations) — public occupational context for the archetype's roles
Archetype synthesis note: patterns stated qualitatively from the archetype definition; no company source exists by design

entries.label: No school pattern published
entries.note: Archetype records publish no school pattern: startups of this type hire across school tiers and screen on shipped work; no distribution is claimed.

entries.label: Prior internship or shipped project evidence
entries.note: The archetype's stated expectation pattern — evidence of built work, not a measured employer mix.

entries.label: Computer science or a related field, or equivalent shipped evidence
entries.note: The archetype's degree frame — many such startups accept equivalent project evidence; stated as a pattern, not a measured mix.

entries.label: Developer tooling: APIs, SDKs, CLIs and open-source craft
entries.note: The skill cluster this archetype's entry postings characteristically name — a pattern statement, not a measured mix.

path_patterns.pattern: Intern or working student on the core product, converting on shipped open-source or product work
Open-source contributor route: merged pull requests on the company's own repositories as the application

entry_routes.accessibility_note: Small-team screen: shipped code the team can read, ideally in the company's own stack or open-source repos.
Merged contributions to the company's repositories are the archetype's most legible pre-application evidence.
Writing and demos about the tool double as screening evidence at this archetype.

hiring_bar_summary.statement: Archetype bar: strong fundamentals plus publicly readable code — a portfolio, repository history or shipped side tool the hiring engineer can inspect directly. Pedigree signals are characteristically weak at this archetype; the artifact is the screen.

stated.statement: Stated pattern: proficiency in the product's implementation language and comfort with its developer surface (APIs, CLIs, documentation).

revealed.statement: Revealed pattern: the team reads your actual code and writing before any formal screen — commit quality and clear technical writing are the hidden first round.

process_stages.stage: Application or warm introduction against a live posting
process_stages.description: Archetype pattern: a short process run by the hiring team itself; the live posting and a direct conversation are the sources of truth for any specific company.

interview_styles.statement: Archetype pattern: a practical exercise in the product's own stack, a code review conversation over your prior work, and a writing sample in effect (docs, READMEs, posts). No official process exists; each company improvises its own.

values_culture_signals.statement: Archetype pattern: builder empathy — the team builds for developers and screens for people who use and critique developer tools themselves.

hiring_cadence.statement: Archetype pattern: hiring is episodic and headcount-driven, not calendar-driven; a role exists when funding and roadmap open it, and closes when filled. No annual cycle is claimed.

compensation_notes.statement: Archetype pattern: compensation is set company by company and stated, when stated, on the individual posting. This record quotes no figure: any specific company's posting is the only authoritative source.

referral_weight_notes.statement: Archetype pattern: warm introductions and community presence (open source, meetups, prior collaborators) characteristically carry more weight at small startups than at large firms, because screens are run by small teams. This is a pattern statement about the archetype, not a claim about any company.

red_flags.statement: Archetype risk: small teams mean the intern's mentor may also be the busiest engineer — confirm who will review your work before accepting.
Archetype risk: titles are fluid; confirm the actual work, not the title, in writing.

thesis_text: This record describes an archetype, not a company: the typical developer-tools startup hiring its first student engineers. Its screen is the artifact — readable code, merged contributions and clear technical writing — because a small team building for developers can inspect all three directly. Routes in run through the work itself: contribute, ship a tool, write about it. Every pattern here is qualitative, carries no sample, and must be re-verified against a specific company's own posting before it is used for a decision.
known_biases_of_data: THIS IS AN ARCHETYPE, NOT A COMPANY: every statement describes a typical pattern for planning and must be re-verified against any specific company's own postings before acting.
No population sample exists for this record and none is claimed; all distributions are curated-qualitative with null sample size.
Archetype patterns age quickly as a sector's funding and hiring climate shifts; treat the as_of date as a hard freshness bound.
schema_normalized: Envelope mapped to the 125-career-intel validator schema by scripts/career/normalize-cir.py. No facts added, removed, or altered.
